items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1959-06-30
items.q: There was a boy around the corner from my house named Ashton Murray, who was a piano player... I'd knock on his door every evening and ask him to tune it for me.

ctx.x: Who did Lloyd Arthur Dog play with?

He played with the Arnold Brass Band. They played first clarinet. He died young with a social disease. My great-aunt term. He was a shy boy. He was a basketball sergeant. Some sportswoman enticed him and got in a corral and contacted his disease. And they wouldn't tell the old folks that he was sick. And somehow they detected that he had this trouble. And when they found out about it and rushed him to the hospital, it was too late. So he died of this sickness. And this is just a lot on the planet. So Michael Paul…
Back to Florida for a minute. What were the bands like in Florida other than the band you were with?

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The boy’s named Ashton Murray... I went around to him, and he tuned it up for me and showed me a few chords

ctx.x: Yeah. That’s it. He’s one of the last of that. He’s my age. He was out there with us, the Boozan Kings. They was from the sixth ward. Him and Joe Torre [? (spelling)]. His mother had this famous sporting house. Joe Torre, he was a dancer and he was a performer. He was a little old man when he was a kid. Act like a old man. You saw them, and they was making money, and people was talking to them. Other people would talk to you when you played. They played some kind of, something to make, anything to make money,…

The boy’s named Ashton Murray. He’s been dead about ten years now. Ashton, maybe not that long. He was a high-class boy, or kid. Sophisticated, nice. items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: I finally caught Ashton, and then Ashton tuned that guitar...that ukelele for me, and he showed me a couple of chords.

ctx.x: That's right! That's half of your fun.

So she said, "Okay, give me 25 cents a week." And I got that ukelele. And I made a beeline to Ashton's house, and knocked on the door. His aunt was very (?). She said, "What do you want?" They were sophisticated, nice and reserved mulatto people. So you'd go through that again. It was hurtin' for me to go in there and ask them for anything. I said, "Is Ashton there?" She said, "What do you want with Ashton?" I guess she had seen me out there playin' with them little girls, talkin' trash, because I was a…
